analysis-results.adoption.definitions: The relational step moves the whole database, a cache step fronts reads and moves no data, and every other step moves one group of queries to one engine; each wave of the roadmap holds one or more steps. analysis-results.help.results-page.title: Results page
analysis-results.help.results-page.body: Choose Info next to a section title to read here what the section shows and how to read it. The section keeps the figures, and this panel holds the explanation.
The roadmap is one suggested order of waves. Each wave shows its gate, and its status says whether the plan suggests that wave.

Tables whose queries are co-dependent move together as one group, and so do tables whose queries a procedure or trigger runs together. A table that a wave's queries read but the wave does not move stays with its owner, and the wave's engine reads a copy kept current from it by CDC.
analysis-results.help.step-scores.title: Step scores
analysis-results.help.step-scores.body: A step's two scores each run from 0 to 1. The step table shows a score with a band as that band, low or high, then its value, and the other score as its value, as the engineering report prints them.
analysis-results.help.close-calls.title: Close calls
analysis-results.help.close-calls.body: A close call is a query that its engine won by only a few points over another engine the plan keeps, which could serve it too. Exact ties that a routing rule settled are listed with them, and the Settled by column says what decided each one.
analysis-results.help.close-calls.review: The assessment still decides each query with its routing rules. You can move any of them yourself in the assignment review.
analysis-results.help.query-flow.title: Query flow
analysis-results.help.query-flow.body: The diagram follows the queries from the source database to the engine each one is assigned to. The wider a band, the more queries it carries.
analysis-results.help.query-flow.cache: A cache layer shows after the engines whose reads it fronts. It owns no query and moves no data. The engine that owns each cached read stays its system of record and keeps every row, so the cache can be rebuilt from it.
analysis-results.help.query-routing.body: Each row is one query and the engine it is assigned to. Select a query to open its detail beside the table, with its history and why it ended on its engine.
analysis-results.help.table-owners.title: Table owners
analysis-results.help.table-owners.body: Each row is one table: its owner, the engines that read a copy of it and, when there is one, the cache in front of its reads.
analysis-results.help.unservable.title: Queries that cannot be served
analysis-results.help.unservable.body: The alert lists queries that no engine can serve as designed. These steps say how to re-run the assessment for them.

graph-explorer.help.title: About the explorer
graph-explorer.help.graph: Source tables are small rectangles with the table icon; destination engines are rounded squares showing the engine's AWS service icon, with its name. Each query is a link from every table it touches to its engine; the queries between one table and one engine are bundled into one straight link until you fan it out into curved per-query links. Link width is traffic (calls per second, on a log scale), and busy links pull their table close to its engine.
graph-explorer.help.click: Click a table or engine to expand it, a bundle to fan it out into its queries, a query link to see its details. Drag a node and its neighbours follow; when you let go it stays there, pinned (a dotted outline), and the rest keeps its place. Double-click a pinned node, or use Unpin in Details, to release it; Reset layout releases them all. The query list on the left follows the graph both ways.
graph-explorer.help.views: Traffic sizes links by calls per second; Moves together marks the queries that move as one unit; Who writes draws each table's writer solid and replica reads dashed; Cost sizes engines by monthly cost.
graph-explorer.help.filters: Filter by engine, by minimum traffic, or by wave: what moves in the wave is drawn in full, the reads its cache fronts a little lighter, the queries that only cut over in it dimmer.
graph-explorer.help.walkthroughs: Walkthroughs follow the assessment's own reasoning: the migration wave by wave and the table groups in each wave, the busiest queries and why each landed where it did, and why each engine. Each step sets the graph; explore from there, then go to the next step.
graph-explorer.help.limits: Waves, units, each table's source of truth, the cache layer and costs are read from the assessment's files with the same code the context graph holds them from. The view draws at most 150 nodes and links. The deliverables and the results page remain the reference.

The toolbar over the graph picks a start point, the view and a query to find; Filters holds the engine, traffic and wave filters. Reset layout puts the panel back.

graph-explorer.help.waves: Picking a wave (as a start point, a walkthrough step or the wave filter) draws what moves in that wave in full, the reads its cache layer fronts a little lighter, and the queries that only cut over in it dimmer. Everything else already in the graph stays visible, greyed out, with its own move wave on hover (and under a greyed engine's name). Thin grey dashed links are cross-wave links: a table in the wave linked to something that moves in another wave, which shows what the wave still connects to. Turn off "Show other waves" in Filters to hide the rest instead.

graph-explorer.help.questions: The Questions tab lists the graph query catalog: fixed, read-only questions about this assessment, such as the busiest queries or what a table's change would touch. Pick a question, choose its parameters from the values the graph holds (or type one when the list is cut short; the server checks it), and run it. The rows show as a table, with how many there are and whether more matched; an empty result says which pipeline stages left nothing to read. Show on graph draws the result as a new start, from its tables first: its own tables and engines are outlined in blue and the links carrying its queries are blue. There is no free-form query.
